**Finding submitted: deviation (low severity, one-line insert).**

- **What exists:** Section 14 (paragraph p0048) already carries a Contractor insurance covenant — workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1M, professional E&O of USD 1M, plus certificates/evidence and notice of material change on Company request. So this is not a "missing clause" case, and it is well clear of walk-away territory.
- **Why it still fails the fallback:** the fallback requires E&O USD 1M **and** cyber USD 2M. E&O is met; cyber cover is entirely absent. That matters here because Contractor's personnel work at Company facilities (§1(c)), access Company computer systems, and handle Confidential Information expressly including "Company records and information" (§8) — so cyber/privacy exposure is real, not theoretical.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** inserted "and cyber liability (including privacy and data breach) insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)" into the existing list — a single in-line addition rather than a new paragraph.
- **Fallback rather than preferred, deliberately:** the whole clause is negotiated at USD 1M levels and there is no defined "Customer Data" processing role, so pressing for USD 5M cyber / USD 2M E&O / USD 2M CGL aggregate would be disproportionate. Those preferred-limit gaps are noted in the rationale, not flagged.
